key_insight: FormalJudge presents a neuro-symbolic oversight paradigm that converts natural-language policies into formal specifications and applies formal verification to certify and correct LLM-agent behavior, reducing reliance on purely probabilistic judgments.
problem_solved: Bridges the reliability gap of the LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm by overcoming the bottleneck of translating human policies into machine-checkable specifications and providing verifiable, actionable oversight for agentic systems.
method: Neuro-symbolic translation: use neural models plus symbolic parsing to convert natural-language policies and agent intents into formal specifications (e.g., temporal logic).
Formal verification: apply model checking / symbolic analysis to agent plans and behaviors against the formal specs to produce pass/fail decisions and concrete counterexamples.

Corrective loop & monitoring: feed verification counterexamples back to agents for repair (replanning, constraint injection, or retraining) and deploy runtime monitors enforcing the synthesized symbolic constraints.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical route to provable, interpretable oversight of LLM-driven agents—improving safety, auditability, and compliance in high-stakes deployments without relying solely on probabilistic judgment.
visual_elements: End-to-end pipeline diagram: Natural-language policy → Neuro-symbolic translator → Formal spec → Verifier → Agent correction loop.
Before/after comparison: LLM-as-Judge (probabilistic, opaque) vs FormalJudge (symbolic specs + formal guarantees).
Spec-translation example: side-by-side natural-language rule and its formal (temporal-logic) encoding with an icon showing automated parsing.
Verification dashboard mockup: pass/fail badges, counterexample traces, and suggested fixes for agent behavior.
paper_title: FormalJudge: A Neuro-Symbolic Paradigm for Agentic Oversight
paper_authors: Jiayi Zhou, Yang Sheng, Hantao Lou, Yaodong Yang, Jie Fu
